entities.name: YC
entities.how_described: 本集围绕 YC 第 47 批开营演讲展开：最初只是想做一家天使投资公司，批次和三个月时长纯属取代暑期工作的偶然产物，后来效果太好就永远这么干了；对『YC 江河日下』的论调从 2008 年就存在，且永远不会停

evidence.quote: So we're here in Mountain View today with PG himself at the original offices doing your talk that you do for the YC batch.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: This is actually the 47th YC batch.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: It's the 21st year also of YC.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: Oops, I better, I'm just talking to YC.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: So you recently posted that the startups YC funds now are much more serious than they were in the supposedly good old days.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: Well, what I meant by supposedly good old days is people are always saying that YC has jumped the shark, you know?
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: YC is always this thing that was great, but now it's not what it was, right?
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: And they're actually really interesting because they helped another YC group.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: It's part of the whole YC community.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: Yeah, using another YC term to attack his cancer.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: And it was incubated at YC.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: I think I already knew that before we started YC because when we started YC, we already had all this experience of doing a startup ourselves, right?
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: And I'm curious, can you tell me a story about a founder where when they started YC, they were maybe not ambitious enough, and then they became very ambitious during the batch?
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: It was quite early on in YC's history when people started applying to YC for the prestige, right?
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: And so these people trying to do YC as a credential.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: And so we already had this word before we started YC, like for a certain kind of person.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: I mean, we already had a kind of startup that we funded in YC, and maybe it has a lot of overlap with what was described in this book, the lean startup, but I haven't actually read it.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: I'm also curious, how does being in a batch like YC give founders an advantage?
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: And another advantage is what we call the YC GDP.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: How did you come up with the idea for YC?
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: How has YC changed or not changed since it's grown?
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: There's a lot more of them, but they, you know, they live in small groups that are just like individual bits of YC.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: So one of the things people saying, when people say YC is jump the shark, one of the things they always say is, oh, it's so big now.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: And if you divide YC up into little bits where each startup is part of a pot of 70 startups, then it's just like they were back in 2012 when there were 70 startups.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

entities.name: OpenAI
entities.how_described: 本集说 OpenAI 是『惊悚级野心』点子兑现的例证——等 Google 的模型过时就能做出新的 Google，PG 用了 OpenAI 之后不再用搜索了，而且它当年是在 YC 孵化的（Sam 众多副业项目之一）

evidence.quote: And that's what OpenAI is, right?
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: Like, I realized very early on, like, after using OpenAI, like, whoa, I don't use Google anymore.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

entities.name: ChatGPT
entities.how_described: 本集用 ChatGPT 早期版本比喻 AI 的反直觉发展路径：不是从完美苍蝇走向人类，而是一开始就得到『一个完完全全的人类，但满嘴胡扯』，像在论文里硬着头皮胡编的本科生

evidence.quote: Like the first AIs, the first versions of ChatGPT were like an undergrad trying to bullshit his way through a paper.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

entities.name: GitLab
entities.how_described: 本集提到 GitLab 的 Sid 得癌症后把治病当初创公司打（『用创始人模式对待我的癌症』），帮他打赢的人后来创办了本批为癌症患者做按需研究的公司

evidence.quote: They helped Sid from GitLab deal with his cancer, which he has done very successfully.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

entities.name: StarCloud
entities.how_described: 本集作为低成本起步的例证：写一份白皮书、预订一次发射就融到了钱——『没有什么比预订一次发射更有说服力』，且其创始人自带领域权威信誉

evidence.quote: Yeah, I think Philip from StarCloud was saying that they basically just wrote a white paper and booked a launch, and they raised the money for StarCloud.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

entities.name: Reddit
entities.how_described: 本集举 Reddit 作为『美好旧时光』YC 投的公司的例子：有价值，但『算不上洲际弹道货物』，用来对比现在这一批的『严肃』公司

evidence.quote: But like in the old days, there was a lot of things like Reddit, right?
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

entities.name: AGI
entities.how_described: 本集说 AGI 原以为是条清晰的终点线，跨过去一切分明；但站上去才发现它有宽度——是一道模糊的 smear，AI 在不同任务上参差不齐，能解数学难题却查不到餐馆营业时间

evidence.quote: So what is the official PG definition of AGI?
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: One of the reasons, one of the ways I knew we were getting close to AGI was I actually had to go and look up the definition of the Turing test.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: Back in the day that AI would be sort of like this finish line and AGI would be this finish line.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

entities.name: 推理 (inference)
entities.how_described: 本集用它论证低成本起步没死：同等推理水平下价格一年大约降 30 倍，token 现在贵只是 GPU 短缺所致，技术总会变便宜

evidence.quote: Certainly inference prices at any given level of inference go down dramatically, like 30x a year or something like that.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

entities.name: 图灵测试 (Turing test)
entities.how_described: 本集说 PG 押图灵测试作 AGI 定义，并称知道自己接近 AGI 的标志之一是他居然需要去查图灵测试的定义了——『我们是不是已经到了？』

evidence.quote: Oh, well, honestly, I mean, could you do better than the Turing test?
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: One of the reasons, one of the ways I knew we were getting close to AGI was I actually had to go and look up the definition of the Turing test.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: Like, what was the Turing test again?
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01
